images.filename: Lost Spring Station Kiosk at Lost Spring, KS (23e7378b50be4d7681835954c366d200).JPG
images.caption:
Lost Spring Station Kiosk at Lost Spring, KS
Lost Spring is 2.3 miles west of Lost Springs, KS on the north side of a paved road. The spring was a valuable source of water, and was also used as a trading ranch, stage station, and campground. The spring still flows and wagon ruts are visible nearby.

images.filename: NTIR Staff walking ruts and swales at Ralph's Ruts in Chase, Kansas (6b2ce29abc7940129983351139fcf4c3).JPG
images.caption:
NTIR Staff walking ruts and swales at Ralph's Ruts in Chase, Kansas
Ralph's Ruts are located west of Chase in Rice County. There is a small public gate near a D.A.R. Santa Fe Trail marker. Looking east, you'll see a series of swales, a set of small hills and valleys, in the natural prairie. These are the prominent Santa Fe Trail ruts. Wagons, mules, and oxen carved the trail into the sandy soil creating the valleys. The "hill tops" are at the original ground level. Convenient roadside parking.
